businessType: Strategy consulting firm serving mid-market manufacturing and industrial clients. 60 employees (10 partners, 35 consultants, 15 support), $18M revenue, 85% realization rate (target 90%).
stage: Growth: $18M revenue (+8% YoY), EBITDA $2.2M (12.2% margin), partner utilization 72% billable (target 75%), junior consultant turnover 18% annually (vs. 10% two years ago). Revenue per employee $300k (below peer average $320k). Junior consultants leaving after 18-24 months; partnership track is narrow (2 partners per 10 hired consultants).
ownerGoal: Return to 15% EBITDA margin and 18%+ revenue growth within 24 months through improved utilization and retention.
ownerConstraints: Junior talent market: Top graduates choosing strategy roles at McKinsey/BCG over boutique firms. Retention poor: 18% turnover, losing to corporate and Big Four moves. Compensation race difficult with large competitors.
Utilization: Partners at 72% billable (vs. peer 75-80%), suggesting bench time or suboptimal project staffing. Consultants' utilization likely lower due to training time.
Client concentration: Top 3 clients = 32% of revenue; client diversification limited. Single client loss would impact revenue 10%+.
Partnership: Only 10 partners; adding partners requires 5+ year track record. Junior-to-partner pipeline weak (18% turnover means most hired consultants leave before partnership consideration).
Market: Boutique consulting consolidating; larger firms (Big Four) expanding in strategy. Differentiation needed; price competition increasing.
immediateConcern: Junior turnover accelerating (10% → 18% in two years) while revenue growth slowing (8% YoY) and margins compressing (moving toward 12% EBITDA from historical 15%+). If turnover continues, firm risks losing institutional knowledge and project delivery capability. Partnership expansion is blocked by weak junior pipeline. Must understand whether problem is compensation (losing to Big Four offers), career path (limited partnership opportunities), or culture/fit.
